articles.title: ‘A terrible, terrible accident’: Cubs’ Bregman undergoing CT scans after taking foul ball to face
articles.summary: Third baseman was standing near on-deck circle. Player taken to hospital for X-rays and CT scan. Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman was taken to the hospital for tests after being struck in the face by a foul ball while standing in front of the on-deck circle during Sunday’s game against the…
body: There was no immediate decision on whether Bregman, who was taken for X-rays and CT scans, would travel with the team back to Chicago after the Cubs’ 9-1 win.

“He got hit in the left cheekbone essentially, under the eye,” Cubs manager Craig Counsell said. “I don’t know anything more than that right now. He was bleeding from his nose a little. There’s some swelling. It’s a terrible, terrible accident. We hope he’s OK.”

In the fourth inning, Michael Busch checked his swing and fouled off a pitch from Reds Luis Mey that struck Bregman, who immediately jogged toward the Cubs’ dugout with his hand covering the left side of his face.
Bregman was escorted by a trainer down the dugout steps and into the clubhouse, with blood visible on his face.

articles.title: Lynx’s Olivia Miles breaks Caitlin Clark’s WNBA rookie scoring record
articles.summary: Guard was named an All-Star in first WNBA season. Miles has broken several records in first campaign. Olivia Miles broke Caitlin Clark’s WNBA rookie scoring record on Sunday in the Minnesota Lynx’s 101-89 victory over the Connecticut Sun.
body: Miles, who finished with 21 points, was tied with Clark at 769 points coming into the game and moved to the top of the list when she made a free throw in the second quarter. The Lynx rookie came into the game averaging 19.7 points, 6.0 assists and 4.7 rebounds, and is a big reason the team have the best record in the WNBA.

“It’s special, but it means we’re more so working well as a team. I have great teammates around me, great vets who allow me to be me out there,” Miles said. “It wouldn’t be possible without one, a coach that believes in you and then two, having teammates that have my back. So it’s really special to obviously be able to accomplish that with such a great team and on a win as well.”

Miles was 7 of 10 from the field and made all six of her free-throw attempts. The All-Star guard, who was selected second in the draft after playing college ball at Notre Dame and TCU, got off to a slow start against the Sun, going scoreless in the first quarter. Her record-breaking free throw came 29 seconds into the second quarter.

articles.title: Evenepoel wins fourth world time trial title in a row, Reusser retains her crown
articles.summary: Remco Evenepoel dominates men’s event in Montreal. Marlen Reusser denies Zoe Backstedt in women’s race. Remco Evenepoel etched his name into the history books with a dominant fourth successive men’s world time-trial victory in Montreal on Sunday.
body: The 2024 Olympic champion came into the race as the overwhelming favourite and he did not disappoint. Evenepoel was already more than 30 seconds ahead of the rest by the second intermediate time check, just over halfway along the 39.2km (24.4 mile) route.

By the time he reached the finish line, the 26-year-old Belgian had put almost a minute into second-placed Filippo Ganna of Italy, with the French rider Paul Seixas taking third another 15 seconds back. Evenepoel has not lost a time trial since the 2025 Tour de France.

Evenepoel becomes the first man to win the time trial world title four times in a row, while also equalling the record number of overall titles held by Germany’s Tony Martin and the Swiss rider Fabian Cancellara.

He has enjoyed his best season to date so far this year, winning the Amstel Gold Race, Clásica San Sebastián and Grand Prix de Québec, as well as finishing second behind Tadej Pogacar this year at the Tour de France.

articles.title: Carrick disputes Cunha’s claim that Manchester United lacked energy in Fulham draw
articles.summary: Michael Carrick insists team ‘kept pushing’ for leveller. Matheus Cunha: ‘Fulham put in more energy than us’ Michael Carrick rejected the suggestion that his Manchester United players lacked physical fitness after they snatched a last-gasp 1-1 draw at Fulham on Sunday.
body: United were poor after the restart at 0-0, leading up to a disastrous Lisandro Martínez own goal in the 63rd minute, with Cunha saying they had to give more. “In the beginning of the second half, Fulham put in more energy than us and we cannot accept this,” Cunha said.

The draw was not the result Carrick or United wanted after a week during which they lost the derby against Manchester City and exited the Carabao Cup against Brighton; both matches were at Old Trafford. Carrick will take it under the circum­stances and he tried to ­highlight the positives which he said took in the never-say-die spirit of his ­players. They fought until the end and were rewarded when ­Cunha’s shot from distance took a heavy deflection off the ­Fulham defender David ­Affengruber to wrongfoot Bernd Leno.

Carrick said he did not agree with Cunha’s comment about the collective energy levels. “I don’t, ­particularly,” the manager said. “The way we finished the game … it didn’t look like that for me. I was quite happy with the way we finished the game. We kept pushing. I don’t think that’s an issue, no.

articles.title: Smith wins World Series of Darts Finals as Littler run ends
articles.summary: England's Ross Smith shocks Wales' Gerwyn Price to win World Series of Darts Finals as Luke Littler's clean-sweep dream ends in last eight in Amsterdam.
body: Englishman Ross Smith won the final six legs to produce a shock 11-5 victory over two-time former winner Gerwyn Price in the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.
It was just a second major title for the 37-year-old, whose only previous success at this level of the PDC World Tour came at the European Championship in 2022.
But the world number 14 overpowered his loftier opponent with a barrage of 180s, hitting 11 maximums, compared to Welshman Price's five, to finish a deserved winner.
It was a fitting finale to a tournament of shocks that saw world champion Luke Littler lose in the quarter-finals and miss out on his quest to claim a clean sweep of the major PDC titles in 2026.

articles.title: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels out for Seahawks game after gruesome injury
articles.summary: Despite missing Sam Darnold for the majority of their first two games, the Seattle Seahawks have started the season with two straight wins and they’re set to take on a shorthanded Washington Commanders squad next, who’s starting quarterback recently suffered an all too familiar injury.
body: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn announced quarterback Jayden Daniels suffered a dislocated left elbow, the same one he injured last season, in the team’s 37-20 Week 2 loss to the Dallas Cowboys. He is set to undergo further testing on Monday, however the initial X-rays eliminated the possibility of a fracture.
Quinn added there’s “optimism” he’ll suit up again this season, although testing should help determine an exact timeline and whether the star quarterback will require surgery.
The injury occurred on 3rd and goal shortly before halftime when Daniels tried to brace himself on the turf after slipping while receiving the snap, and landed awkwardly.

It’s a crucial blow for the third-year quarterback who’s coming off an injury riddled 2025 campaign where he suffered a knee sprain and hamstring injury before the disastrous dislocated elbow in Washington’s 38-14 loss to the Seahawks. Daniels missed three games after the previous elbow injury.

articles.title: 49ers game grades: A Purdy good day on offense helps put Dolphins away
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers crushed the Miami Dolphins by a final score of 35-13 Sunday, very much as expected, but there were multiple key performances that helped seal the outcome - and say perhaps even more about the team's readiness to keep rolling. Offense: A.
body: Giving up a long, late meaningless 77-yard touchdown pass to get the Dolphins into double digits on their last possession wasn't a great note to finish on, but Raheem Morris' defense delivered four sacks (including rookie Romello Height's first) and five tackles for a loss against Miami. And while the Dolphins aren't good, both of Miami's second-quarter field goals came after the 49ers' defense stymied them in the red zone, which was when the outcome was far from certain; better to bend than break. Safety Ji'Ayir Brown led the way with 13 total tackles, while Dre Greenlaw netted five solo tackles, matching his single-season high with the Broncos last year.

Whatever was ailing kicker Eddy Piñeiro over the past week wasn't a factor, as he nailed all five extra points, while punter Corliss Waitman buried the Dolphins inside the 20 on both of his kicks. The Dolphins netted an average of 25 yards on their kickoff returns, which might sound like something, but it's around last season's average across the NFL. A competent day in the office, which fans and the 49ers will take after the heartache before special teams coordinator Brant Boyer was brought in last season.

articles.title: Middlesex beat Leicestershire to end 36-year List A trophy wait
articles.summary: Middlesex ended a 36-year List A trophy drought by beating Leicestershire Foxes by 31 runs to win the Metro Bank One Day Cup in a low-scoring final at Trent Bridge.
body: Ryan Higgins made a superb maiden List A hundred from 115 balls with Harry Duke (55) backing him up as their 135-run sixth-wicket partnership steered Middlesex from 71-5 to 231 all out after Foxes all-rounder Ian Holland took 5-36 and wicketkeeper Ben Cox held five catches. Higgins and Duke were making their first appearances for Middlesex in this year's competition.

New Zealand international batter Nick Kelly hit an equally brilliant 103 (107 balls) to lead a Leicestershire fightback from 79-5 but it was not enough to haul his side over the line, Tom Helm (3-32) claiming his vital wicket in a superb late spell as the Foxes were bowled out for 200.

In an impressive performance in the field by Middlesex, Toby Roland-Jones (3-27) showed his quality and 21-year-old pace prospect Naayva Sharma (3-37) finished as the competition's leading wicket-taker with 20.
Against a background of turmoil off the field, the win is a first for Middlesex in a List A final since they beat Derbyshire to lift the 1990 Refuge Assurance Cup.

articles.title: Brittany and Patrick Mahomes Share a Kiss in Sweet Moment Before Chiefs Game
articles.summary: NEED TO KNOW. Patrick and Brittany Mahomes shared a pregame kiss before the Chiefs faced the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, Sept. 20. Brittany was rocking the Chiefs’ signature red color as she supported her husband at Arrowhead Stadium. The Chiefs won their first game of the season on Monday, Sept.
body: Patrick Mahomes shared a sweet kiss with his wife, Brittany, before the Chiefs hosted the Indianapolis Colts in Week 2.

Just before kickoff on Sunday, Sept. 20, Brittany made her way to the sidelines to show support for her quarterback husband — who returned to the field on Monday, Sept. 14 after tearing both the ACL and LCL in his left knee last season — and wish him good luck with a kiss.

Mahomes was dressed in his Chiefs uniform and headband as he met his wife on the sidelines. Brittany, 31, made it clear she was ready to cheer on the Chiefs by wearing the team’s signature red color to Arrowhead Stadium.

Mahomes, who celebrated his 31st birthday on Sept. 17, scored the first touchdown in the Chiefs’ home opener against the Denver Broncos last Monday. The quarterback ran the ball into the end zone in his first game back from injury and celebrated his team’s win — and his return to the field — afterwards on social media.

articles.title: Smith thrashes Price to win World Series after Littler's shock exit
articles.summary: Ross Smith thrashed Gerwyn Price 11-5 to become World Series of Darts Finals champion, while Luke Littler's hopes of a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 were dashed in the quarter-finals.
body: Smith won the last six legs, fired in 11 maximums, recorded back-to-back ton-plus finishes and went at 46 per cent on his doubles as he overwhelmed Price in Amsterdam on Sunday night to claim his second PDC major, after the 2022 European Championship.

Price, who missed a host of doubles in the back end of the match as his checkout percentage dropped to 26, has seven PDC majors in total, including three Grand Slams and the 2021 World Championship, but none since the World Series Finals in 2022.
Speaking bluntly afterwards on ITV4, the Welshman said: "I am playing some good darts, I am earning some good money. If I never win a major again I really don't care as long as I am doing well.

"I am gutted I've lost but if I never win another major then I have a good family, I have invested all my money. I really don't mind. I will be gutted for half an hour but on Tuesday I'll be in Tenerife.

articles.title: 'I deserve to be in!' - Spaun uses Team USA snub as fuel for Wentworth win
articles.summary: JJ Spaun said he played with a "huge chip on his shoulder" during his BMW PGA Championship win and used being snubbed by Team USA's Presidents Cup side as motivation for his Wentworth victory.
body: Spaun became the first player since Byeong Hun An in 2015 to win the DP World Tour's flagship event on debut, posting a final-round 67 to claim a two-shot success over Rory McIlroy, Aaron Rai, Adam Scott and Manuel Elvira.

Last year's US Open champion also won on the PGA Tour earlier this season at the Valero Texas Open and finished 10th in the Presidents Cup qualification standings, having also made his Team USA debut in the Ryder Cup last September.

Spaun was controversially overlooked for a captain's pick by Brandt Snedeker in his line-up to face the International Team in the biennial contest, live from Thursday on Sky Sports, with the 36-year-old pleased to respond by claiming a statement victory.
"The stars aligned this week for me to come out on top," Spaun said. "I'm just grateful to have the opportunity and play well and give myself a chance and came out with a W.
